newsitem.title: FINLAND: LUNDH WANTS NEW NUCLEAR PLANTS, PULP, PAPER MILLS.
newsitem.headline: LUNDH WANTS NEW NUCLEAR PLANTS, PULP, PAPER MILLS.

text.p: Two new nuclear power plants, two new pulp mills and five new paper machines should be built in Finland during the next 10 years, metal workers' union chairman Per-Erik Lundh said on Friday.
"Finland needs its own home-made survival programme. This programme should rest solidly on a determined industrialisation of Finland," Lundh told a seminar according to a copy of his prepared speech.
"In the next 10 years we build two new nuclear power plants. At the same time, we build tens of quite small regional plants producing heating and electricity by burning wood," he said.
"Two new pulp mills supplying five new paper machines," he added.
Such a programme could create up to 25,000 new jobs, Lundh added. Industry's share of GDP should rise to 40 percent. It was 28.6 percent in 1995, up from 28.3 percent in 1994.

Annual research and development expenditure should be raised to five percent of GDP from the government's current target of two percent. This would boost the development of innovative new products and raise the degree of product refinement and so help prevent Finland from becoming a low-wage area, he said.
This would reqire venture capital and other financing arrangements, Lundh said. The state's revenue from sales of state-controlled companies should be used as venture capital.
"The crown jewels should not be wasted on consumption, but used for investments which create new wealth," he said.
By implementing the industrialisation programme, the Finnish metal industry could employ 210,000-220,000 people 10 years from now compared to 170,000 currently.
